newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on spillover weakness.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on spillover weakness.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended lower on spillover from weakness in other U.S. wheat markets, but traders said the nearby March contract was buoyed by bull-spreading tied to tight deliverable stocks.
U.S. wheat futures weakened amid fading fears of winterkill in the U.S. winter wheat crop.

But tight deliverable stocks of spring wheat helped cushion the kinds of losses seen in Chicago and Kansas City. The MGE reported Tuesday that deliverable spring wheat wheat stocks in Minneapolis as of January 10 were 1.649 million bushels, versus 1.926 million last week and 4.312 million last year.
Traders said logistical problems caused by severe winter weather had kept basis levels firm, which contributed support in the nearby contract.
MGE spring wheat closed one to 8-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with March down one cent at $3.92-1/2. May was down 3-3/4 cents at $3.72-1/4.
Traders said LFG sold at least 500,000 March bushels.
MGE barley settled eight to 10 cents per cwt higher, with March up 10 cents at $6.75.
